criteria.criterion: In docs/spec.toml, requirement OLY-B-NOTE-01 has a mechanism that is no longer "none" and names crates/athena-core/src/status/planning.rs (`specialization`) and crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs, both of which exist (Grep for the names); its owner stays Athena; its measure says how it is shown and ends with `status: specialization`, a heading line that display.rs prints in `athena status`.
criteria.evidence: Read docs/spec.toml lines 2431-2438. The mechanism names `specialization` in crates/athena-core/src/status/planning.rs and crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs. Owner is "Athena". The measure describes the seeded test and the real-records check, and ends with `status: specialization`. Grep shows `pub fn specialization` at planning.rs:488 and `fn specialization_lines` at display.rs:185, which prints the line starting "specialization   per class of work…" (display.rs:192). The label ("specialization","specialization") is in STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS (status.rs:313).

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a new test (for example in crates/athena-cli/tests/routing_evidence.rs) builds fixture records where a non-baseline producer model/effort has at least SPECIALIZATION_MIN_JOBS jobs and a higher landed share, and asserts the status text prints the `specialization` line with that setting flagged as helping. The test fails if the specialization call or its display is removed, and passes with it.
criteria.evidence: Both new tests passed. The first seeds 4 failing `medium` jobs (the baseline) and SPECIALIZATION_MIN_JOBS (3) landing `high` jobs. It asserts that a line starts with "specialization " and that the text contains "code: specialization helps: m · high beat the default". The same test first asserts that the block is absent when there are no records. By reading the code (I could not edit files to try it): removing `out.push_str(&specialization_lines(...))` at display.rs:1338 breaks the line assertion, and an empty `specialization()` result breaks `view.specialization.len() == 1`. So the test fails without the mechanism. The second test checks that 2 jobs give "not enough jobs" and no flag. The CI run also passed the full test suite.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot <evidence directory>` on the real records: the `specialization` block lists each class of work, and its per-setting job counts sum to the number of dispatched request jobs with a producer invocation. The expected range comes from counting those jobs in history.json and the recorded invocations, a source the change does not compute. Any class flagged as helping has at least 3 jobs in that setting.
criteria.evidence: Run on the evidence snapshot. The block lists 7 classes: build, code, config, design, docs, prompts, tests. The per-setting job counts sum to 767 (5+559+38+50+58+31+26). I counted independently in the evidence records with Grep. There are 856 job.json files with "kind": "request" (dispatched request jobs), so 856 is the upper bound. There are 867 producer invocation files, and some jobs have more than one producer run. There are 692 verification.json files; the block's verified counts sum to 688, and a verified job must have had a producer run. So the expected range is about 688–856, and 767 falls inside it. The block's landed counts sum to 474, against 476 landed jobs overall in the same output. I did not compute an exact distinct-job count (the tools allowed could not dedupe file paths), so the range is an estimate from these counts. Flagged settings and their job counts: code sonnet·high 193, prompts haiku·unrecorded 3, tests sonnet·unrecorded 7. All have at least 3 jobs. These figures describe the evidence snapshot, not the live records.

findings.summary: Existing figure: 'unrecorded' effort counts as a setting, and 3 jobs is a low bar to flag
findings.evidence: On real records, 'tests' is flagged because `sonnet · unrecorded` beat the default, and 'prompts' is flagged on 2 of 3 landed. 'unrecorded' groups older invocations whose effort was not kept, not a setting anyone can choose. This behavior predates this change and is within the accepted reading. A later change could leave 'unrecorded' out of the flag or require a margin.

summary: This change passes. Requirement OLY-B-NOTE-01 in docs/spec.toml now has a mechanism: the existing `specialization` figure (planning.rs) printed by display.rs. Its owner is still Athena, and its measure ends `status: specialization`, a label that `athena status` prints. The new test file crates/athena-cli/tests/routing_evidence.rs passed when I ran it. It seeds records, checks that a setting with 3 landing jobs is flagged as helping, and checks that 2 jobs are not flagged. Reading the code shows it would fail if the specialization block were taken out of the status output. I ran `athena status --snapshot` on the evidence records: the block lists 7 classes, and their per-setting job counts sum to 767. That falls within an estimated range of about 688 to 856, taken from my own count of request job files, producer invocation files and verification files in the snapshot. Every flagged setting has at least 3 jobs. The recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed, and no figure module changed. There are two minor findings. First, two files changed outside the deliverables list, snapshot.rs and shard-timings.txt; both were needed. Second, the new `--snapshot` output has no test. A nit about the existing figure counting 'unrecorded' effort as a setting predates this change.
